reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant (stepwise) signal with robust-standardized values ranging roughly from -1.5 to +1.5, exhibiting a dominant period of ~332 points (1 cycle per 332 points), consistent with the estimated period. Each cycle contains one sharp negative spike (trough) followed by a slower positive ramp-up and a plateau; the troughs are narrow (~1–3 points wide), deep (~−1.0 to −1.5), and consistently preceded by a flat segment at moderate positive levels (~+0.8 to +1.2). After the trough, the signal rises in 1–2 steps to a new plateau, often slightly higher than the prior one, indicating a weak cumulative upward drift across cycles. Amplitude (90th percentile range) varies between ~2.3 and 3.0, reflecting modest inter-cycle variation in peak-to-trough span. Noise is negligible—no high-frequency jitter; transitions are clean step changes. Baseline level shifts gradually upward over long horizons (slope per point near zero but slightly positive in longer windows), yet within any single 3P or 5P window the trend is nearly flat. Morphology is highly repeatable: each cycle shows the same sequence—plateau → sharp drop → recovery → new plateau—with consistent relative timing of the trough (~30–40% into the cycle) and recovery slope. Acceptable variation includes ±0.2 in plateau height, ±0.3 in trough depth, and ±10 points in trough timing; deviations beyond this suggest anomaly.

Overall highly consistent with shorter candidates; minor irregularity does not invalidate normality.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 1 (3P, high reliability) for queries with 2–4 clear cycles; use its trough timing and recovery slope as primary template. For single-cycle queries, align to reference 0 but allow ±10-point trough shift and ±0.2 amplitude tolerance. For longer queries (>4 cycles), use reference 3’s drift profile but downweight the region near index 2200; if query shows similar minor dip without recovery, treat as potential incipient anomaly. When query morphology deviates in trough width (>5 points) or lacks stepwise recovery (e.g., smooth ramp), flag as anomalous regardless of amplitude.
